my, as part of address formulas, is used as an element that can modulate both the solidarity and power dimensions of the relationship between the speaker and the addressee, depending on the address terms it modifies.
my is an element which has a functional import, but its meaning is not always the same, as it depends on the address term which it modifies.

the use of my in address formulae is not a mere matter of politeness, but rather a complex phenomenon which depends on the interaction between the speaker and the addressee and the specific context in which the interaction takes place.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the alternation of dear and my dear and the use of my with my lord/lady or your lordship/ladieship in the eight British English plays investigated in this paper are not random, but rather have functional import. Dear, my dear, your dear.

the use of my in address formulae is not random, but rather follows a set of rules which depend on the speaker's intention to convey a certain power or solidarity meaning, and on the speaker's perception of the power and/or solidarity relationship with the addressee.
the alternation between my dear and dear, as well my lord/lady, and your lordship/ ladyship, is motivated by the power dimension and by the solidarity dimension, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of my can be seen as an indicator of the speaker’s desire to establish a close relationship with the addressee.
, although my is not a prototypical address term, it may be used as a modifier of other address terms to convey a specific pragmatic function.

, in the investigated data, my is used as an address term to express power and solidarity, which is consistent both with previous research and with the findings of other studies of address terms in other languages.
